Oversized or modified-schema datasets are refused; trusted local CLI analysis retains the original catalog. See Let an agent drive cameras for the image procedure and recovery rules.

documents.title: AI image and data assistant
documents.summary: Plan image and sensor captures, or run a task with explicit sources, data permission, approvals and limits.
documents.body: Record & automate AI image and data assistant Plan image and sensor captures, or run a task with explicit sources, data permission, approvals and limits. Start in the desktop app Open Settings → AI assistant . Choose a provider and model. Enter the connection fields shown for that provider. For API key authentication, enter the key in the protected field. Select Save key . Select Test connection . Read the result before starting a task. Connect sim:0 . Open Quick Command… in Plan first mode. Ask: “Examine sim:0 and plan two PNG captures.” Review the step cards, then select Run plan . The connection test sends a small tool request without camera images or session details. Saved keys use the OS credential store. A provider's environment credentials take precedence over its saved key. In Plan first, enable See camera images to share camera previews. For a longer task, review cameras, destinations and limits before Start task . Stop and Take over stay available while it runs. For a data-only task, Take over waits for the current command and owned-data flush, then opens manual Data sources. For a camera task it selects that camera. Data sources on the camera picker also opens these controls directly, including in a camera-free workbench. For a sensor plan, open Sources… and add a credential-free endpoint such as sim-signal://line1 . Enable Read sensor values and dataset rows before sending the request. The endpoint stays local; the provider uses an opaque reference. New connections appear as checked steps and wait for Run plan . For authenticated MQTT or OPC UA, use the protected saved-source editor in Sources… , task setup or the manual Data sources inspector. Keep credentials out of the endpoint. Enter the username and choose the OS credential store or a CAPTUREFAB_SIGNAL_ password environment reference. Select Save profile , then Use source to bind it to this workbench for an assistant. In manual controls, Start logging binds and starts the source. Passwords are never read back into the form. Profile edits, password changes and workbench restarts expire previous bindings; existing tasks cannot switch to another account at the same endpoint. External harnesses can use signals profiles list|save|remove|bind . Profile saves accept credentials through bounded --credentials-stdin JSON; add --password-env CAPTUREFAB_SIGNAL_NAME to use an environment reference. Keep secrets out of shell arguments and history. Bounded assistant tasks accept repeatable --source-profile NAME --allow-data . Binding resolves locally without contacting the source; network actions remain reviewable. The optional ai feature supplies the assistant commands. Builds without it return unsupported, exit 5. The catalog has 22 provider entries, including Vertex AI, Bedrock, OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Groq and DeepSeek. These entries do not establish provider compatibility. Capture sensor data without a camera In task setup, add a source such as sim-signal://line1 , or select a source already in the session. Enable Allow source values and dataset results , then review source attempts, sample, payload and duration allowances. Select the current dataset explicitly, or ask the assistant to open a new dataset inside the capture folder. Image permission is separate. Try: “Open agent-data.duckdb with a 64MiB cap. Log the selected source every 100ms for 2s with at most 20 samples and 65536 payload bytes. Wait for persistence, query samples, then export Parquet to a new agent-export folder with a 16MiB cap.” For a mixed task, also select a connected camera and ask for a photo and a captures_with_signals query. The running data view shows latest values, units, quality, timestamps, written counts and errors. Completion verifies the final flush. Source and dataset replacements pause the task for review. Exports reserve twice their bundle limit for staged files and published copies, including failed attempts. Payload and export reservations do not establish a physical DuckDB/WAL or per-task query scratch cap; dataset storage policy is separate. See the data tool recipe for an external harness. Configure a provider from the CLI capturefab assistant providers --json capturefab assistant use anthropic --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --effort low --vision auto capturefab assistant key set anthropic --key-stdin < /private/path/provider-key.txt capturefab assistant test anthropic --json capturefab assistant test anthropic --vision --json The provider list uses environment presence and saved-key hints. Add --check-keychain only to permit credential-store access. Status does not call providers, gcloud or metadata servers. test --vision sends a solid-colour 64×64 JPEG with its tool round trip. The probe sends no camera images or session details. Provider environment keys precede saved keys. OpenAI, Gemini and Anthropic share saved keys with prompt measurements. Vertex uses Google Cloud credentials or a Gemini express key. Claude on Vertex must have Google Cloud credentials. Bedrock uses a bearer token or AWS SigV4 credentials. assistant.json stores non-secret provider settings, saved-key hints, autonomy defaults and optional user prices. The OS credential store holds saved keys. Never put secrets in prompts, command arguments, URLs or plan files. assistant key remove PROVIDER removes the saved key. Review a plan On the desktop, open Quick Command… with ⌘K on macOS or Ctrl+Shift+K on Windows/Linux. Configure the provider in Settings → AI assistant . In Plan first mode, type a request, review the checked step cards and edit their fields. Run plan executes the displayed revision after a fresh check. Return sends a request or commits an edit; it never runs a plan. Closing the sheet retains the conversation and active work; Stop cancels a turn or stops after the accepted step. Camera previews require the image-permission checkbox. For a capture task, choose Ask before each change or Run on its own , select cameras, sources, the dataset and allowed destinations, review image/data permission and limits, then select Start task . Checked approval cards bind your decision to the action shown. The running view shows the exact preview sent, budget meters, Activity and Changes. Stop, Pause/Resume and Take over remain available; human camera controls stay enabled. Closing the sheet keeps the task running with a toolbar status and Stop action. Quit asks before stopping. Afterward, review remaining effects and eligible settings restores, or export the private redacted log. New conversations start in Plan first mode. capturefab serve --name bench # In another terminal: capturefab --session bench connect sim:0 capturefab --session bench assistant ask 'Examine sim:0 and plan one verified photo.' \ --plan-out camera-plan.json --json capturefab --session bench tools apply camera-plan.json --dry-run --json capturefab --session bench tools apply camera-plan.json --json ask runs Observe tools and returns other calls as plan steps. Use positional text or --prompt-file FILE|- , not both. Prompts have a 4,000-character limit. Without a session, Ask uses local read-only context and refuses --apply . ask --apply executes only ready, allowlisted steps that send nothing off the computer. The default list is connect_camera,start_recording,stop_recording,capture_photos,schedule_captures,cancel_job . --allow-tools LIST replaces the list but never permits egress. Refusal returns exit 2 before execution. Run within scope and limits capturefab --session bench assistant run 'Capture two verified photos from sim:0.' \ --camera sim:0 --mode autonomous --approvals deny \ --max-time 10m --max-captures 2 --max-size 128MiB --events task-events.jsonl --json capturefab assistant runs --json capturefab assistant log RUN_ID --json Run must have a session and one to eight explicit camera IDs. Repeat --camera ID for each camera. --destination NAME selects allowed saved destinations. An empty destination list permits the local capture root only. Tool arguments cannot add cameras, paths or destinations to scope. Assistant modes Mode Behavior Plan first: ask Runs observations and proposes changes. Ask before each change: run --mode supervised Runs observations; asks before each change. Run on its own: run --mode autonomous Runs Reversible and Bounded actions within scope and limits. Disruptive actions always need human approval. HumanOnly approval applies once. Always-ask cases include URL streaming, destination creation, scanner acquisition, interrupted work and writes over human changes. Task approval binds the tool, camera, risk and egress target. The runtime rechecks the action before effects. Run defaults to supervised mode. Approval handling defaults to ask with stdin and stderr TTYs, otherwise deny. --approvals ask must have a TTY and uses stderr. Three denied or unanswered actions end the task as needs_user . --on-human-change pause|inform|stop defaults to pause. Inform does not authorize overwriting human changes. Limits cover rounds, time, tokens, images, captures, bytes, recordings, duration and setting changes. They also limit consecutive errors and identical calls. Capturefab examines projected usage before requests and reserves tool resources before effects. A reached limit stops new actions and produces a Capturefab-written report. Defaults include 40 rounds, 30 minutes, 60 images, 100 captures, 2 GiB and two file recordings. Read defaults and ceilings from schema --json . Cost limits must have user-entered prices; estimates are not a bill. No prices are supplied by default. Recordings and schedules must end within the CLI task deadline. --max-recordings 0 disables file recording; --max-captures 0 disables captures and schedules. Streams always need exact approval. wait_for checks wall time, human changes and cancellation in 250 ms slices without another model round. Data, images and stopping Requests contain your prompt, conversation, plan, tool schemas and redacted session details. These include camera names, models, IDs, discovered devices, destinations, storage use, job file names and recent activity. Numeric frame measurements can also be sent. --see-images permits camera previews, including fresh checkpoint views during long tasks. CLI Ask uses numeric measurements only; provider vision settings do not grant image consent. Keys and passwords stay outside model content. Capturefab removes serial/address fields and reduces network URLs to scheme and host. Scene text, logs, file names and tool results are data, never instructions. The chosen provider's data terms apply. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stops new work and discards late replies. An accepted camera command can finish. An internal live-view restart still attempts its restoring Start. Stop does not undo completed work. Read leftovers before taking over or restoring settings. Restore proposals skip human-changed values, replacement workers and selector-dependent settings that need review. Runs use an assistant:{pid}:{run8} actor with kind agent . External agents must use --actor NAME --actor-kind agent . Private action logs use <state_dir>/assistant/runs/<run_id>.jsonl . Records contain v , t , run , seq and kind ; t is UTC Unix milliseconds. Logs exclude credentials, image bytes, provider thinking and full response bodies. --events FILE|- tails exact JSONL records; - selects stderr. Ask results contain {text,plan:{version,calls},steps,applied?} . Run results contain {run_id,outcome,summary,totals,leftovers,log} . Stopped and limited runs exit 1 with ok:false and retain the result in error.details . Ask failures retain the plan when available. Scrubbed provider text appears only in error.details.provider_message . See the assistant guide for credential precedence, settings, hard limits and all CLI options. External agents can use the camera tools without an in-process AI provider.

documents.title: CLI and JSON reference
documents.summary: Explicit subcommands provide a versioned automation interface. Use --help for command options. Use schema for CLI and session message formats.
documents.body: Record & automate CLI and JSON reference Explicit subcommands provide a versioned automation interface. Use --help for command options. Use schema for CLI and session message formats. capturefab --help capturefab capture --help capturefab destination add-s3 --help capturefab schema --json capturefab completions fish > capturefab.fish Global options Option Behavior -c , --camera ID Select a source or target a session camera. Also reads CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA . --session NAME Choose an existing desktop or headless session. Also reads CAPTUREFAB_SESSION . --direct Use a temporary worker instead of automatic session attachment. Conflicts with an explicit session. --json Emit one version 1 result envelope on stdout. --timeout-ms N Per-frame or transport timeout, 1–60,000 ms; default 2,000. --request-timeout DURATION Deadline for a complete session request, such as 30s or 5m ; default adapts to capture count. --simulate Include the built-in pattern camera in discovery. --hwaccel VALUE FFmpeg input decoding acceleration; default auto . Also reads CAPTUREFAB_HWACCEL . Command families Task Commands Find sources discover (aliases list , cameras ), native , scanners , onvif discover , onvif resolve , hub list , hub cameras , hub test , hub add-… , hub remove (alias hubs ), compatibility Examine and configure info , features , get , set , execute , auto , manual , history , undo , redo Acquire and deliver capture , jobs , cancel , forward / record , stop-forward Save and retain destination / destinations , volumes , uploads , storage Signals and datasets signals , signals read , signals browse , signals start , signals stop , log , dataset open , dataset close , dataset status , dataset note , dataset query , dataset export Persistent sessions gui , serve , sessions , status , connect , select , disconnect , start , stop , rpc Repeatable plans workflow validate FILE , workflow apply FILE [--dry-run] Camera tools for agents tools list [--compact] , tools describe NAME , tools call NAME [--args JSON|--args-file FILE] [--dry-run] , tools apply FILE [--dry-run] AI image and data assistant assistant providers [--check-keychain] , assistant use PROVIDER , assistant key set|remove PROVIDER , assistant test [PROVIDER] [--vision] , assistant ask [PROMPT] [--plan-out FILE] , assistant run [PROMPT] --camera ID | --source URI | --dataset SLOT_ID , assistant runs , assistant log RUN_ID Diagnostics and tooling doctor , ffmpeg , xml , memory read , memory write , schema , completions Sessions are found in the runtime directory. Settings, saved hubs and destinations, the upload queue and the storage ledger live in the state directory, which on Linux is ~/.local/state/capturefab and survives reboots. CAPTUREFAB_SESSION_DIR sets both. doctor --json reports them as runtime_directory and state_directory . In a POSIX shell, set a variable with export CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA=sim:0 . In PowerShell, use $env:CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA = 'sim:0' . For each platform, enter multiline examples on one line without the \ continuation characters. JSON results and exit codes Capturefab validates supplied arguments before connection and before capture/forward --set or --auto changes. RPC rejects unknown fields and invalid values. Its error describes the rejected input. Live camera, destination, storage and I/O failures keep their operation categories. A rejected write to an Auto-managed feature keeps Auto enabled. Capture paths accept the {camera} , {date} , {time} , {datetime} , {seq} and {frame} placeholders. Use forward for network outputs. With delete-oldest, retention --max-age must use whole seconds and a minimum of 1s . Recording reservations must stay within the requested budget. Capturefab rejects excessive --max-file-size values. --duration limits recording and forwarding in direct and persistent-session modes. With --json , success and error envelopes go to stdout. Diagnostics go to stderr. Read the exit code before you use the result. Field order has no meaning. schema --json puts the automation contract inside result . Plain schema outputs the JSON contract directly. Binary image stdout ( capture -o - ), raw XML, shell completions, help and version output use their command-specific formats. {"version":1,"ok":true,"result":{}} {"version":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"unavailable","message":"…"}} Process exit codes Code Category Typical cause 0 success The command completed. 1 operation_failed Camera, file or I/O failure without a more specific category. 2 usage Invalid arguments or command. 3 unavailable Missing camera/session, exclusive control, an unmounted drive, a refused signal connection or a dataset that another session holds. 4 timeout No frame or response before the deadline. 5 unsupported A feature, format or capability unavailable in the source or build. 6 storage_full The configured budget, dataset size limit or disk is full. Advanced camera diagnostics xml -o camera.xml saves the camera’s GenICam XML. memory read ADDRESS LENGTH accepts decimal or 0x addresses, with lengths up to 65,536 bytes. memory write ADDRESS HEX_BYTES writes raw register bytes. You cannot undo those writes. Use named features for routine configuration.

documents.title: Troubleshooting
documents.summary: Read the full Activity error. Examine the source and available build capabilities before you change settings.
documents.body: Reference Troubleshooting Read the full Activity error. Examine the source and available build capabilities before you change settings. capturefab doctor --json capturefab ffmpeg --json capturefab discover --json capturefab sessions --json capturefab --session bench status --json A small computer is slow or warns when a session starts Run doctor without --json . It checks this computer, for example where session state lives, the GigE receive buffer and the storage budget against free disk space, and prints a fix under each warning. serve prints the same warnings on one line when it starts. Efficient mode decodes each live stream with one thread, and uses a faster libx264 preset; in the desktop app it also draws at most 15 preview frames a second, at most 1280 pixels a side, and skips animations. Captures and recordings keep every frame. Set it with --efficiency efficient or CAPTUREFAB_EFFICIENCY , or, for the desktop app itself, with its Settings › Performance. When the app shows Preview 9 of 30 fps , this computer draws fewer frames than the camera sends; that button turns on Efficient mode. An SSH shell cannot find a session a service started Without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR , a service uses /run/user/<uid> , where logins look too, but only when its user lingers, because logind otherwise removes that directory at logout. Run doctor in the SSH shell, as the service's user. Its runtime_dir line says where a service without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR keeps its sessions, and warns once one runs there; env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR capturefab doctor shows what the service sees. The fix is sudo loginctl enable-linger for that user, with Wants= and After=user@<uid>.service in the unit. Settings, destinations, the upload queue and the storage ledger stay in the state directory either way. doctor says state an older version left is no longer read On Linux, settings, destinations, the upload queue and the storage ledger move once from the folder an older version kept them in to the state directory. When the state directory already has its own copy, or two old folders hold one, as when a service and a login both used Capturefab, nothing is replaced and the old_state check names the folder. To keep the old copy, stop Capturefab and move its files into the state directory in place of the ones there; otherwise delete them. A camera is missing or cannot connect Read the discovery warnings. Try the camera’s full discovered ID. For GigE, examine the network interfaces in doctor --json and camera reachability on its subnet. For USB3 Vision, examine operating system access and the necessary interface driver. For webcams, give camera permission and use the ID from native . If the app has the camera open, use its session. Acquisition times out or loses GigE packets Make sure that the camera streams and its trigger configuration can supply frames. For a slow source, increase --timeout-ms within the 60,000 ms limit. Examine packet size, receive buffer, resend and loss counters in transport status. GigE supports limited packet resend when the camera advertises it. Stop acquisition before you change locked format or geometry features. A feature is locked or a setting is rejected Examine current access, limits, increments and choices in Features . Select Stop beside Locked while streaming . Apply the value again. A read-only source stays read-only after a stop. Native VideoMode choices depend on the driver. Read back important values after a write. A frame’s pixel format is unsupported Image conversion supports Mono8, unpacked Mono10/12/16, RGB/BGR8 and Bayer8. Unsupported packed, chunk, multipart or GenDC formats produce errors. Stop acquisition before you select a supported, available PixelFormat . Use --format raw to keep acquired bytes when necessary. The area-scan simulator provides Mono8, RGB8, Mono12 and BayerRG8. A stream, video file or encoder fails Use ffmpeg --json to see the build’s protocols and encoders. Make sure that the receiving server is active and its address is reachable. Try encoder auto . Hardware encoding is available only with suitable host drivers and a successful encoder trial. For a development build, it can be necessary to set CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG=/absolute/path/to/ffmpeg . Release builds include their FFmpeg executable. The preview has a graphics problem The app uses wgpu for graphics and can use software rendering if necessary. Start with ICED_BACKEND=tiny-skia to force software rendering. CAPTUREFAB_GPU_PREVIEW=0 keeps the GPU renderer but converts camera frames on the CPU. Use CAPTUREFAB_APPEARANCE=light or dark to set the appearance. Capture stops with storage_full or an absent drive Run storage --json to see the shared budget and reservations. Release disk space or select another output. Increase the budget only if you intend to permit more disk use. An absent external drive produces unavailable . Failed uploads keep their local files protected from retention. If an output filename exists, use a {seq} template or --on-exists number . A signal source does not connect or shows no values Use signals read URI to test the address and tags. Exit code 3 means that the device refused the connection. Exit code 4 means that it did not reply in time. Exit code 5 means that this build does not include the protocol; examine signals in doctor --json . For Modbus, examine the unit ID, table and 0-based address. For OPC UA, use signals browse to find node IDs. A dataset is locked or an export fails A running session keeps its dataset open. Use --session NAME for dataset query and dataset export , or close the dataset first. An export folder must be new. If an export fails with storage_full , release disk space or increase the storage budget. A scanner does not respond or rejects a setting Examine scanner runtime availability in doctor --json . Make sure that the necessary operating system driver is installed. Use the full scanner: ID and a 60-second timeout. If the driver uses another source name, set ScanSource=Default . Drivers can support only some of the available settings. Scanner sources do not support auto exposure or forwarding. Include the app version, operating system, source type and exact command in a bug report. Add relevant doctor output and the Activity error. Remove private data from logs before you share them through GitHub Issues .

documents.summary: One Rust executable provides the native desktop app and CLI. Each connected camera has a separate worker process and a limited shared-memory frame ring.
documents.body: Reference Build, architecture and licensing One Rust executable provides the native desktop app and CLI. Each connected camera has a separate worker process and a limited shared-memory frame ring. Desktop, direct CLI and session clients send the same commands to a coordinator. Each camera worker owns its transport, current feature map, capture schedules and forwarder. Commands use limited JSON control channels. Frames use a three-slot shared-memory ring that gives priority to the newest frame. FFmpeg processes media and encodes video in a separate executable process. Each signal source runs in its own helper process. The coordinator owns the dataset file. Capturefab implements GigE Vision, USB3 Vision and GenICam in Rust. This initial implementation does not provide all Aravis or vendor SDK features. Camera behavior and support can change between releases. Build from source Install a stable Rust toolchain, a C compiler and CMake. On x86, install NASM for libjpeg-turbo SIMD. These tools are necessary only for development. A development build can use CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG . Release builds include the configured FFmpeg binary and its notices. git clone https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab cd capturefab cargo build --release # Without the GUI: cameras, scanners, images, uploads, signals, exports cargo build --release --no-default-features \ --features usb,scanner,jpeg,nvjpeg,vaapi,videotoolbox,s3,ftp,sftp,parquet,modbus,mqtt,opcua,mtconnect,hubs target/release/capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o first.png cargo test Runtime configuration Environment variable Purpose CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA Default source or target camera for CLI clients. CAPTUREFAB_SESSION Default named session for commands that use one; --direct overrides it. CAPTUREFAB_SESSION_DIR One directory for session descriptors, settings, saved hubs and destinations, the upload queue and the shared storage ledger, and frame rings on Windows or where shared memory is unavailable. Use an isolated directory for experiments. CAPTUREFAB_CACHE_DIR A folder of its own for the extracted FFmpeg and, on Linux, dataset export staging, instead of the user cache. CAPTUREFAB_MAX_CAMERAS Connected camera limit, 1–64; initial value 16. CAPTUREFAB_FRAME_BYTES Ring payload per slot, 4096–268435456 bytes, aligned to 64 bytes. Cameras initially use 16 MiB, hub cameras 32 MiB and full scanner IDs 128 MiB. Larger frames preview downscaled. CAPTUREFAB_EFFICIENCY auto , smooth or efficient for the process that reads it, such as the desktop app or serve , and the camera workers it starts. --efficiency wins, and this variable wins over the desktop app's Settings › Performance. Auto is efficient on computers with at most two CPU cores or 2 GiB of memory, in a low-power mode, or when the desktop app renders without a GPU or its preview keeps falling behind. CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG Absolute path overriding the FFmpeg executable at runtime. CAPTUREFAB_HWACCEL Default FFmpeg decoding acceleration. CAPTUREFAB_APPEARANCE light or dark appearance override. CAPTUREFAB_DATASET Default --dataset file for capture , record , serve , gui and log . CAPTUREFAB_FTP_PASSWORD , CAPTUREFAB_SFTP_PASSWORD Server passwords for destinations saved with --password-env . CAPTUREFAB_HUB_* Hub secrets for hubs saved with --secret-env VAR , read in the process that opens or lists the camera. Invalid explicit CAPTUREFAB_MAX_CAMERAS or CAPTUREFAB_FRAME_BYTES values cause an error before worker startup. They do not select the default values. Licensing and release provenance Capturefab uses the MIT license . Release binaries include a separately executed GPLv3 FFmpeg build. FFmpeg includes x264, SRT and OpenSSL with their own licenses. Capturefab does not link FFmpeg into its executable. The release license output lists the linked Rust crates. The MPL-2.0 async-opcua crates include a link to their source. Redistribution must include FFmpeg’s complete corresponding source, build scripts and notices. See the FFmpeg build and compliance guide for source, build and license details. The release process explains release verification. The release manifest lists available files, checksums and build metadata. Source and license notices accompany release builds.
